chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim, from ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Bashīr, from Sulaymān ibn Hilāl, who said:
Some of our companions asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who has intercourse with a beast,
So he said: “He is made to stand upright, then he is struck with a blow of the sword; whatever the sword takes from him, it takes.”
He said: So I said, “Is it killing?” He said: “That is so.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the authority giving the ruling
key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man being asked about in the legal case
key_terms.الْبَهِيمَةَ: the animal with which the prohibited act is committed
key_terms.الْقَتْلُ: killing; the questioner’s clarification of the ruling
key_terms.ضَرْبَةً بِالسَّيْفِ: a blow with the sword as the mode of execution
key_terms.يُقَامُ قَائِمًا: he is made to stand upright for the execution of the punishment

ai.seo_question: What punishment does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām mention for a man who has intercourse with an animal?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Imām Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام concerning a man who commits intercourse with an animal. The Imam عليه السلام states that the prescribed punishment is death by the sword, and the questioner confirms that the ruling means killing.
